HTML Form Integration

Updated October 9, 2026
文AAlso available in:Deutsch,Español,Français,Italiano,日本語

Connect any static HTML form to MyFormCapture in under two minutes. You don’t need PHP, Node.js, or any server-side logic — simply point your form’s action attribute to your unique MyFormCapture endpoint.

What you’ll build

Section titled “What you’ll build”

In this guide, you will create a standard contact form with three inputs:

  1. Name (<input type="text" name="name" />)
  2. Email address (<input type="email" name="email" />)
  3. Message (<textarea name="message"></textarea>)

When visitors submit this form on your website, MyFormCapture captures the submission, runs spam filtering, sends you an email notification, and forwards the data to any configured webhooks.

File structure

Section titled “File structure”

Place your HTML form inside your standard website project directory:

Project Workspace
my-website/
├── index.html           ← Form markup goes here
├── styles.css           ← Optional form styling
└── assets/
    └── logo.svg

Complete HTML form example

Section titled “Complete HTML form example”

Copy and paste the code snippet below directly into your index.html file:

index.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<title>Contact Us — MyFormCapture Demo</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
<main class="container">
  <h1>Contact Our Team</h1>
  <p>Fill out the form below and we will get back to you shortly.</p>

  <!-- 1. Replace 'demo-form-uuid' with your real form ID from your dashboard -->
  <!-- 2. Keep method set to POST -->
  <form action="https://myformcapture.com/f/demo-form-uuid" method="POST">
    
    <!-- Name Field -->
    <div class="form-group">
      <label for="name">Your Name</label>
      <input 
        type="text" 
        id="name" 
        name="name" 
        placeholder="Jane Doe" 
        required 
      />
    </div>

    <!-- Email Field -->
    <div class="form-group">
      <label for="email">Email Address</label>
      <input 
        type="email" 
        id="email" 
        name="email" 
        placeholder="jane@example.com" 
        required 
      />
    </div>

    <!-- Message Field -->
    <div class="form-group">
      <label for="message">Message</label>
      <textarea 
        id="message" 
        name="message" 
        rows="5" 
        placeholder="How can we help your team?" 
        required
      ></textarea>
    </div>

    <!-- Optional: Custom redirect URL upon successful submission -->
    <input type="hidden" name="_next" value="https://yourwebsite.com/thank-you.html" />

    <!-- Optional: Honeypot field for bot protection (keep hidden) -->
    <input type="text" name="_gotcha" style="display:none !important" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" />

    <!-- Submit Button -->
    <button type="submit" class="submit-btn">Send Message</button>
  </form>
</main>
</body>
</html>

Step-by-step explanation

Section titled “Step-by-step explanation”
1

Set the Form Action URL

The action attribute points directly to your unique MyFormCapture endpoint. Each form in your dashboard receives a dedicated UUID such as https://myformcapture.com/f/your-form-uuid.

2

Specify the POST Method

Always configure method=“POST”. MyFormCapture processes incoming form data over secure HTTPS POST requests.

3

Assign Descriptive Input Names

MyFormCapture maps submission columns directly from each input’s name attribute (e.g. name=“name”, name=“email”, name=“message”). Make sure each field has a unique name.

4

Add Custom Redirect & Spam Prevention

Adding <input type=“hidden” name=“_next” value=“https://…”> automatically redirects users back to your custom thank-you page. Adding name=“_gotcha” acts as a silent honeypot that catches automated spam bots.

Illustrative Demo Endpoint The endpoint https://myformcapture.com/f/demo-form-uuid is an illustrative placeholder. In your actual production deployment, replace this placeholder with your authentic form endpoint from your MyFormCapture console.
